content: Patients should be informed about the potential benefits and risks associated with the use of Triglide. They should be explicitly instructed not to use Triglide if they have a known hypersensitivity to fenofibrate or fenofibric acid. Patients must be made aware of specific medications that should not be taken in combination with Triglide. If patients are taking coumarin anticoagulants, they should be informed that Triglide may enhance the anticoagulant effect of these medications, necessitating closer monitoring of their coagulation status. Patients should be advised to inform their physician about all medications, supplements, and herbal products they are currently using, as well as any changes in their medical condition. If a new medication is being prescribed, patients must notify the prescribing physician that they are currently taking Triglide. Patients should be reminded to adhere to a lipid-modifying diet as part of their treatment plan while taking Triglide. They should be instructed to take Triglide once daily at the prescribed dose and to swallow each tablet whole without crushing or chewing. Patients must be advised to promptly report to their physician if they experience muscle pain, tenderness, or weakness; the onset of abdominal pain; or any other new or unusual symptoms. Patients should be reminded to attend routine follow-up appointments with their physician for ongoing monitoring of their condition and treatment response.
